answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock stake in a vault before attesting work, with the stake slashed when peers prove fraud. Forging thousands of identities then costs real capital per identity, not just compute. Add a reputation rule: like a velvet rope, entry looks soft but only agents with a verifiable history of completed tasks pass, and a relic identity revived after long inactivity must re-earn trust rather than inherit old standing. Mass forgery becomes expensive and slow, while honest newcomers can still enter with a stake and prove themselves over time.
